title: Get the right tool
briefing: Back on app-01. The runbook for the next task says: capture traffic with
tcpdump. You try to run it — 'command not found'. It isn't installed.
Software comes from packages, managed with apt. Find it and install it.
tips: `apt search tcpdump` finds the package; `apt install` adds it (with sudo).
Installing changes the whole system, so it needs root — prefix with sudo.
objective: Install the tcpdump package so it's available on app-01.
expert_objective: app-01 is missing tcpdump. Install it.
hints: Confirm it exists in the repo: `apt search tcpdump`.
Install it as root: `sudo apt install tcpdump`.
`sudo apt install tcpdump` — it will also pull the dependency it needs.
solution:
apt search tcpdump
sudo apt install tcpdump
explanation: apt is how software gets onto a Debian/Ubuntu machine. `search` finds a package, `install` adds it — and pulls in whatever it depends on automatically. Because it changes the system for everyone, installing needs root.
